analysis:
Docs-only change. Examined the cli-reference.md head excerpts (lines 1289-1888) and the quickstart.md patch and base text. No code, auth, crypto, or coordinator/provider protocol is changed in the supplied evidence. The cli-reference excerpts show no changed lines (changed head ranges are near lines 14-16, 781-825 and 1885). Those hunks fall outside the supplied excerpts, so their patch was only partially visible.

The security-relevant behavior change is described, not implemented here. Quickstart.md (head ~65-71, 109-116) and the cli-reference patch say Autopilot, once enrolled, adds every verified downloaded catalog build to its set with no new consent step. They also say Autopilot may download catalog models on the operator's behalf. Limits come from `darkbloom autopilot downloads enable --max-storage-gb N --max-models N`, and downloads can be turned off with `darkbloom autopilot downloads disable`. The docs state it never deletes files.

Relevant threat IDs are A-004, T-012, T-027 (model weight integrity and substitution), T-016 (disk fill) and T-029/T-003 (resource use). The docs claim the added builds are verified catalog builds. I could not check that claim, so I did not treat the change as a regression.

Open questions for the code reviewer:
1. Whether auto-downloads go through the same weight-hash and integrity verification as `darkbloom models download`, including the catalog fetch and hash source.
2. Whether the default download limits are bounded or unbounded when the operator has not set them, which matters for disk-fill and unattended-bandwidth impact.
3. Whether the implicit inclusion of newly downloaded models in Autopilot's set at next provider start changes which models are advertised to the coordinator without explicit operator selection.
4. Whether the threat model's TB-007/A-004 text should record Autopilot-initiated downloads as a new weight-acquisition path.

The unchanged prefix-cache/T-041 statements in the cli-reference excerpts are pre-existing and not altered by this PR. No finding is raised because the implementing code is not in the supplied evidence.
